title: Label test: 40 of your past comments
description: Item 27, 23 Nov 2026. Label each comment yourself. Claude labelled all 40 first, and its key is saved and kept off this page.
intro: Pick the label for each comment, the way you meant it at the time. Claude labelled all 40 before this page was built. Its key is kept off the page, so your picks stay blind. When you are done, the results come back test-style: each comment, your label, Claude's label, and the match rate per label.
The six labels, from the brain:
Content: what is said. Facts, quotes, built details, missing material. Yours: "where the fuck did healthy come from?"
Structure: where things go. Order, joins, repeats, gaps, sections, headings. Yours: "this point seems to be repeated too much"
Intention: what a part is for. The point, what the reader should get, whether a part earns its place. Yours: "I want to allude to it and build hype to it."
Tone: how you come across to the reader, and how you feel about the subject. Yours: "I don't like the advice and diagnosis and knowitallness"
Wording: how it is put into words. Word choice, sentence build, choppy lines, slop. Yours: "what is this vague metaphor no one ever uses?"
Mechanics: grammar and marks. Yours: "oxford comma important"
None of the comments here are the examples used to define the labels.
